# C2.2 Common World canonical source publisher identity

Phase 2B-5AI-P explicitly adds wire `monaka-wire-2.2` to C2/C2.1. This
contract supersedes no existing 2.1 field or message. C1's prohibition on adding
required fields to an existing minor-version message is preserved by adding six
messages in a new namespace, following the C2.1 new-message precedent.

## Message boundary and version

`monaka.common_world_identity` has the six existing Common World type names:
world_authority, mapping_publication, common_pose, common_unavailable,
mapping_revocation, world_revocation. Each has version major 2, minor exactly 2,
the corresponding C2.1 payload, and required top-level `source_publisher_id`.
Unknown versions fail with UnsupportedVersion. The old namespace remains
`monaka.common_world` and has unchanged 2.1 encoding/validation semantics.

The new field is the canonical upstream Trusted Source Authority publisher_id,
never the Bridge envelope publisher_id, source_id, owner epoch, source session,
generation, transport session, endpoint, or inferred default. Id syntax is
inherited: case-sensitive opaque nonblank UTF-8, 1..96 UTF-8 bytes, no control
characters, no normalization. JSON escaping does not change the identity.

All six messages expose owner_id and coordinate_space.id through world or
mapping.world, and expose source_publisher_id explicitly at top level. Together
these provide the stable owner/world/source publisher association tuple.
Ephemeral values retain their distinct C2.1 meanings.

## Pure model and compatibility

The C++ and JVM Common World public models have an additive nullable
source_publisher_id property. Null explicitly denotes a legacy decoded message.
A present value selects the new namespace and requires version 2.2 on encode.
A legacy-namespace packet never acquires publisher identity, even if an unknown
optional field happens to be named source_publisher_id. Its decoder ignores that
field. Encoder output with a null property remains byte-identical to C2.1.

| Encoder | Decoder | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1 legacy | 2.1 | unchanged |
| 2.2 identity | 2.2 | explicit canonical publisher preserved |
| 2.2 identity | 2.1 | UnsupportedMessage, new namespace |
| 2.1 legacy | 2.2 | legacy model, null publisher |

Publisher-aware production publication/association requires identity-capable
2.2 messages. Consumers must reject null identity where that trust is required.
No receiver runtime, association store or application ACK is introduced here.

## Encoding and bounds

The production codecs retain canonical sorted JSON, strict UTF-8, duplicate-key
rejection, depth limit 16 and whole-datagram 4096-byte bound. Required field,
type, framing, truncation, invalid identity and size failures leave decode
output unchanged. No IP-fragmentation requirement is added. All numeric fields,
binary64 exact-copy rules, coordinate conventions and owner/world semantics
remain C2.1. Deterministic new golden vectors supplement the frozen 2.1 vectors.

Authorization must bind the immutable publisher to the revision before enqueue,
persist it in an explicitly versioned record/receipt where restart publication
is supported, and validate current authorization before send without rewriting
the identity. Legacy records cannot be upgraded by guessing a publisher.
